commitResults.messageBody: Move command input and all user-facing output out of Slay69 so the main class can focus on coordinating application behaviour. Preserve the existing messages and command flow while giving later command objects a single interface for interacting with the user.

commitResults.messageTitle: Encapsulate tasks in TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList as the owner of task collection operations instead of exposing a mutable ArrayList throughout the application. Update Storage to return loaded tasks and accept a general read-only List when saving, which keeps persistence separate from task management and supports a configurable file path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse commands into executable objects
commitResults.messageBody: Add a Command hierarchy for add, list, mark, unmark, delete, and exit operations, and move input interpretation into Parser. Keep task-number range checks inside TaskList and reduce Slay69 to the application lifecycle and parse-execute loop, completing both the A-MoreOOP minimum and command-class stretch goal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store new deadline dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody: Parse ISO deadline dates at the command boundary, format them for display, and persist them in ISO form. Keep loading and saving earlier free-text deadline values so existing user data remains accessible after the date upgrade.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody: Parse find queries into a dedicated command, search task descriptions without case sensitivity in TaskList, and display matches using their original task numbers so users can act on the results. Report missing keywords and empty result sets clearly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the chatbot public API with Javadoc
commitResults.messageBody: Add class, constructor, and method documentation across tasks, commands, parsing, storage, and UI. Explain task numbering, persistence behavior, and command errors so the generated API reference is useful to future maintainers; complete missing parameter and return descriptions for clean doclint output.
